_doc: Stream E (play-test 2, Q18). Quests and quest NPCs of the set pieces near Torborhold (data/vignettes/setpieces.json). A PART of zone `test` (the Torbor Fields): merged into data/quests/test.json via its `include` list. NPC `at` = a set piece id (the placer stands them inside it). Same quest format as data/quests/README.md.

corporal_jenk.name: Corporal Jenk
corporal_jenk.greeting: Sergeant says I'm to keep the dummies in good repair. I say the dummies started it.

hesketh_brannock.name: Hesketh Brannock
hesketh_brannock.greeting: Mind the wheat. Mind the turnips. Mind the scarecrow, he's had a hard week.

ada_orchard.name: Ada of the Orchard
ada_orchard.greeting: The apples are early, the bees are cross and the cider is nearly a crime. Lovely season.

hob_turnwater.name: Miller Hob Turnwater
hob_turnwater.greeting: If you hear squeaking, it's the wheel. If you hear squeaking and chewing, it's not.

abel_fenn.name: Sexton Abel Fenn
abel_fenn.greeting: Come to visit someone? Everybody here is in. Nobody's going anywhere. Usually.

kit_greyfletch.name: Kit Greyfletch
kit_greyfletch.greeting: Uncle Oswy does the big hunts. I do the tally board. One day the tally board will do me.

bettony.name: Bettony the herb-woman
bettony.greeting: Step round the mushrooms, dear. They hold grudges against feet.

pilgrim_orla.name: Orla the pilgrim
pilgrim_orla.greeting: I walked here barefoot from Mill End. In hindsight, a mistake.

warden_maddoc.name: Warden Maddoc
warden_maddoc.greeting: Coldharrow was a fine house once. Now it's a fine place to get stabbed.

edda_ashby.name: Foreman Edda Ashby
edda_ashby.greeting: Every tree we fell, the forest sends something to complain about it.

old_wat.name: Old Wat the fisher
old_wat.greeting: Forty years at this pool. The croakers have been here a fortnight and they think they own it.

drover_gil.name: Gil the drover
drover_gil.greeting: Have you seen an ox? Big, brown, looks disappointed in you? That's Duchess.

quests.name: Practice Makes Bruises
quests.offer: New in town? The Sergeant won't look at anyone who hasn't been round the yard. Hit the dummy, put three in the butts, walk the sand. Then you're one of us. Mostly.

steps.text: Thrash the straw dummy
steps.where: Torbor Drill Field, just outside Torborhold

steps.text: Shoot at the archery butts
steps.where: the far end of Torbor Drill Field

steps.text: Walk the sparring ring
steps.where: the sand pit at Torbor Drill Field

quests.done: Not bad. The dummy will need a new head, but not bad.

quests.name: Scarecrow Duty
quests.offer: Two boars come out of the hedge every evening and dig my turnips like they're paid to. The scarecrow does nothing. Help him out.

steps.text: Kill 4 thicket boars around Brannock Fields
steps.where: the turnip patch and hedges of Brannock Fields

steps.text: Tell the scarecrow it's over
steps.where: the scarecrow in the wheat at Brannock Fields

quests.done: There. He looks taller already. Take this, and some turnips, they're only a little bitten.

quests.name: Cider for the Watch
quests.offer: The reeve in Torborhold pays for cider in favours, and I'm owed a few. Press me a jug and carry it to Reeve Corwin. Don't drink it on the way. Well. Not much of it.

steps.text: Press a jug of cider
steps.where: the cider press in the orchard at Brannock Fields

steps.text: Bring the cider to Reeve Corwin
steps.where: Reeve Corwin, in Torborhold

quests.done: The reeve said thank you? Out loud? Gods, it's strong this year.

quests.name: Rats in the Grist
quests.offer: The rats in my grain store have grown bold. One sat on the scales and looked at me. Thin them out before they start charging rent.

steps.text: Kill 6 cairn rats at Turnwater Mill
steps.where: the grain store behind Turnwater Mill

quests.done: Quiet. Lovely, chewing-free quiet. Here, for your trouble.

quests.name: Open the Race
quests.offer: Now the rats are gone I can hear the wheel properly, and it sounds wrong. Open the sluice full and look at the gearing while it runs. I'm too old to climb.

steps.text: Open the sluice
steps.where: the sluice on the mill race at Turnwater Mill

steps.text: Look over the gearing
steps.where: the gear housing inside Turnwater Mill

steps.text: Tell Hob what you saw
steps.where: Miller Hob at Turnwater Mill

quests.done: New oak teeth? I never put those in. Somebody's been mending my mill at night. Should I be grateful or afraid?

quests.name: Diggers in the Yard
quests.offer: Barrow hounds. They dig for what's buried and they are not fussy about whose it is. Drive them off before Mrs Thatcher's husband ends up in the hedge again.

steps.text: Kill 4 barrow hounds in Saint Hulda's Yard
steps.where: among the graves of Saint Hulda's Yard

quests.done: Everyone is back where they belong. Thank you. They can't say it, so I will.

quests.name: Ring for the Dead
quests.offer: The hounds came for a reason. Something under the yard calls them. Old custom: ring the bell, knock at the ossuary, and bring me a pinch of the dust they carry. Then we'll know what wakes.

steps.text: Gather 3 pinches of grave dust from barrow hounds
steps.where: barrow hounds in and around Saint Hulda's Yard

steps.text: Ring the sexton's bell
steps.where: the bell frame by the lychgate of Saint Hulda's Yard

steps.text: Knock at the ossuary door
steps.where: the ossuary at the back of Saint Hulda's Yard

steps.text: Bring the dust to Sexton Abel Fenn
steps.where: Sexton Abel Fenn in Saint Hulda's Yard

quests.done: The dust is warm. Dust should not be warm. I'm going to need a bigger spade, and a priest.

quests.name: Tallies for the Board
quests.offer: The moor hounds have been bold since Gristle took the packs. Uncle wants six more on the board before he'll take anyone after the big one. Go on — I'll chalk them up.

steps.text: Kill 6 moor hounds
steps.where: the open grass between Torborhold and Greyfletch Camp

steps.text: Chalk your kills on the tally board
steps.where: the tally board at Greyfletch Camp

quests.done: Six! In your own column and everything. Uncle will pretend he isn't impressed.

quests.name: The Fairy Ring
quests.offer: The croakers down at Tench Pool carry spawn that the stones like. Don't ask me how I know. Bring me some, walk round the mushrooms — round, mind — and pour it on the altar.

steps.text: Gather 4 croaker spawn from fen croakers
steps.where: fen croakers in the reeds at Tench Pool

steps.text: Walk round the ring of mushrooms
steps.where: the fairy ring inside the Nine Maidens

steps.text: Pour the spawn on the altar stone
steps.where: the altar at the centre of the Nine Maidens

quests.done: There — did you feel them shift? No? Good. You're not supposed to. Here's a little something from the stones.

quests.name: Stones for the Mother
quests.offer: Brigands robbed the shrine — took the painted prayer stones, thinking they were worth something. They're not, except to everyone who painted one. Get them back?

steps.text: Take back 4 painted prayer stones from road brigands
steps.where: road brigands along the roads and at Coldharrow Ruins

steps.text: Return the stones to the cairns
steps.where: the prayer cairns at the Shrine of the Kind Mother

quests.done: Every one back where it was. "Let him come back" — that's mine. Thank you.

quests.name: Squatters at Coldharrow
quests.offer: Brigands have made a camp in the east wing. Bold, burning the furniture of a house that already burned. Clear them out.

steps.text: Kill 6 road brigands at Coldharrow Ruins
steps.where: the brigands' fire on the east side of Coldharrow Ruins

quests.done: Gone. For now. They always come back to a roof, and this place doesn't even have one.

quests.name: The Coldharrow Fire
quests.offer: Thirty years and nobody knows how the fire started. I have a guess. Climb what's left of the stair, then look at the circle in the hall — don't stand in it — and tell me I'm wrong.

steps.text: Climb the collapsed stair
steps.where: the broken stair against the tower at Coldharrow Ruins

steps.text: Look at the cracked circle in the hall
steps.where: the old hall floor at Coldharrow Ruins

steps.text: Tell Warden Maddoc what you found
steps.where: Warden Maddoc at Coldharrow Ruins

quests.done: From the inside, then. The daughter. I knew it. And she's still about, they say. Keep your shadow close.

quests.name: Bats in the Timber
quests.offer: Dusk flitters roost in the log stacks and come out screaming whenever we start sawing. My cutters won't work the last hour of light. Sort it.

steps.text: Kill 5 dusk flitters at Ashby's Lumber Camp
steps.where: the log stacks at Ashby's Lumber Camp

quests.done: Quiet stacks. My lads will work till dark now, whether they like it or not.

quests.name: The Missing Saw
quests.offer: Our good two-man saw went to Old Wat at Tench Pool to cut new jetty planks, and it never came back. Fetch it, and give the pit a proper run so I know it's still true.

steps.text: Ask Old Wat for the saw
steps.where: Old Wat at Tench Pool

steps.text: Work the saw pit with the returned saw
steps.where: the saw pit at Ashby's Lumber Camp

quests.done: Still sings. Wat's a thief, but he's a careful thief.

quests.name: Croakers in the Keepnet
quests.offer: Croakers. In the reeds, in my traps, in my keepnet. One of them ate a tench bigger than my arm and then looked at me like I owed it the other half.

steps.text: Kill 6 fen croakers at Tench Pool
steps.where: the reeds round Tench Pool

steps.text: Reset the fish traps
steps.where: the fish traps on the bank at Tench Pool

quests.done: Peace on the water. I may even catch something. Here — and don't tell Edda I still have her saw.

quests.name: Who Moved Duchess?
quests.offer: Duchess wandered off in the night. Big brown ox, deep sense of grievance. Last I heard she was eating someone's wheat. Find her, and find whose wheat.

steps.text: Look for Duchess at Brannock Fields
steps.where: Brannock Fields, north of the inn toward Torborhold

steps.text: Ask Hesketh Brannock about the ox
steps.where: Hesketh Brannock at Brannock Fields

steps.text: Tell Gil where Duchess is
steps.where: Gil the drover at the Pail and Plough

quests.done: Eating the wheat AND sleeping in the barn? That's my girl. I'll pay Hesketh for the wheat. Mostly.
